Is Dell Stock Priced Right Against Its Peers?

Dell Technologies (DELL) stock trades at a lower price-to-earnings ratio than four of the five companies on its Trefis peer list: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, IBM, Cisco Systems and Apple. Yet over its latest four quarters, Dell grew revenue faster than all five, HP Inc. included. So is Dell's lower price a bargain for that growth, or a sign the market expects it to fade?

You Pay Less For Dell's Faster Growth

Dell trades at 19.0 times its earnings over its latest four quarters, compared with 22.9 for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, a company in the same hardware industry whose four quarters also ended on July 31, 2026. At that lower price, you get faster growth: Dell's revenue rose 49.0% over those quarters, against 26.6% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Dell also kept more of its sales as operating profit, posting a margin of 9.6% against 7.8%.

HP is the one company in the group that costs less than Dell, at 10.7 times earnings, and its revenue grew 8.1%. Every other peer costs more than Dell and grows more slowly, so Dell ranks first of the six on growth and second cheapest on price.

Most Of Dell's Growth Comes From Servers And Storage

Dell operates two main businesses. The Infrastructure Solutions Group sells servers, storage and networking, while the Client Solutions Group sells PCs. In fiscal 2026, which ended on January 30, 2026, infrastructure revenue rose 39.5% to $60.8 billion, while PC revenue grew 5.4%.

The latest quarter followed the same pattern. Management said infrastructure revenue rose 89% to $31.8 billion in fiscal Q2 2027, which ended on July 31, 2026. AI servers alone brought in $16.4 billion, and Dell ended the quarter with a record $95 billion of AI orders still to ship.

Dell's operating margin ranks fourth in the group, behind Apple, Cisco Systems and IBM. AI servers appear to earn less on each dollar of sales than the rest of what Dell sells. Management expects Dell's gross margin rates for fiscal 2027 as a whole to be up from a year earlier once the effect of the AI server mix is left out. Even so, Dell's operating margin over the latest four quarters is its highest at any of the 40 quarter ends since fiscal Q3 2017. Management names scale as the single biggest reason for the improvement.

Accenture (ACN) stock returned 55.3% over the six months to November 10, 2026, against 2.2% for the S&P 500. Yet management has guided for revenue growth of only 3% to 6% in local currency in fiscal 2027, and the low end allows for clients cutting back on discretionary spending. The table below lists the events most likely to move Accenture stock in the next six months, and the first report date among them comes in December.

Against the stock

Accenture's First-Quarter Report In December

Accenture is expected to report its fiscal Q1 2027 results in December 2026, marking the first quarter under the new guide. Management's guide for that quarter is revenue growth of 2% to 6% in local currency, after 7% in fiscal Q4 2026. The report will also show how quickly recent orders become sales. Accenture booked $22.2 billion of new work in fiscal Q4 2026, and managed services bookings reached a record for the company. Management said on the October 1 call that its large deals add work over several years. Revenue growth in local currency against management's guide for the quarter is the figure to watch in the December report.

Clients' Technology Budgets For 2027

For most Accenture clients whose financial years end in December, budget cycles were only starting at the time of the October 1 call, so management expects to know more in January and February. For now, management assumes more of the same. The top of its fiscal 2027 range allows for stable to slightly improving discretionary spending, while the bottom allows for it to get worse. With currency expected to make little difference, the two ends of that range are about $2.2 billion of sales apart, on fiscal 2026 revenue of $74.2 billion. IBM is expected to report in January 2027 and Cognizant in February 2027, and their revenue growth will be an early read on those budgets from Accenture's peers.

Lower Prices On Accenture's Work

Lower prices are already showing up. Management said on the October 1 call that pricing was overall stable across fiscal 2026, but that fiscal Q4 2026 brought lower pricing in many areas of the business, in a highly competitive market. On the same call, management said Accenture is giving clients more productivity because of AI and more than making up for it with new kinds of work and wider scope. The fiscal 2027 guide is an operating margin of 15.9% to 16.1% on management's adjusted measure, only 10 to 30 basis points above its adjusted fiscal 2026 margin, so that guide could be harder to reach if lower prices spread. Management said on the same call that its margin guide already assumes continued intense competition. Accenture's December 2026 report will show whether management keeps that margin guide.

Pure-play quantum stocks have plunged 41% to 65% in a year as technical milestones fail to translate into sustainable commercial revenue.

Rigetti's revenue fell 28% while its operating loss ran about 24 times sales, and D-Wave's spending topped revenue twelvefold.

IBM, Intel, and Nvidia can profit from quantum's manufacturing, software, and classical computing needs without betting on one winning processor architecture.

Pure-play quantum stocks have lost 41%–65% over the past year even as hardware milestones advance.

Rigetti and D-Wave earnings expose the gap between technological progress and sustainable commercial revenue.

IBM, Intel, and Nvidia may benefit from the infrastructure and manufacturing requirements of quantum computing without depending on a single winning processor.

Quantum Computing's Investment Problem Is Becoming Clearer

The quantum computing industry is confronting a distinction between technological progress and commercial profitability. Processors are improving, yet recent results suggest that useful systems are advancing faster than sustainable business models. This raises an investment question: will the developers of quantum processors capture the largest profits, or will established semiconductor and computing companies benefit more from the infrastructure needed to make quantum computing practical?

The latest earnings provide a useful test. D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) reported just $4.5 million in third-quarter revenue despite substantial nine-month bookings growth. Rigetti Computing (RGTI) reported a 28% revenue decline to $1.4 million. IonQ (IONQ) reported $173.8 million in revenue, but nearly half came from acquired SkyWater foundry operations. These are materially different forms of commercialization.

Funtap / Shutterstock.com

Meanwhile, IBM (IBM) is deploying integrated quantum systems, Intel (INTC) is pursuing silicon spin qubits and quantum software, and Nvidia (NVDA) is positioning its accelerated computing infrastructure to support multiple quantum architectures. Their financial exposure differs fundamentally from that of the pure plays.

title: Is Accenture Stock Becoming A Different Bet?
detail:
Is Accenture Stock Becoming A Different Bet?
Trefis Team

ACN
^GSPC
IBM
CTSH
BAH
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Accenture (ACN) stock costs you 18.3 times its earnings over the last twelve months, compared with 21.8 for the S&P 500, so you will want to know what growth you are buying. In September 2025, management had a clear answer: on its fiscal Q4 2025 call, the company said it had tripled its revenue from Gen AI over fiscal 2024. Management no longer emphasizes that figure. So what does management point to now?

Accenture Now Makes Its AI Case Through Partners

During the fiscal Q4 2026 call on October 1, 2026, management pointed to Accenture's partners. Calling the company's strong ecosystem position one of the reasons it is so confident about the AI opportunity, management said Accenture's top 10 ecosystem partners represented more than 60% of revenue in fiscal 2026.

That is a different kind of figure from the one management gave before. On its fiscal Q1 2026 call in December 2025, management put a dollar figure on advanced AI revenue for the quarter and called it another milestone. A dollar figure like that shows how much revenue Accenture brings in from AI work on its own. A partner share counts the revenue from all of Accenture's work with those partners, and that is most of the company.

How Big Are Accenture's AI Sales Against Partner Sales?

Accenture's AI sales accounted for close to 6% of its revenue in fiscal Q1 2026. Management put advanced AI revenue for that quarter at about $1.1 billion, out of $18.7 billion in total.

Revenue from one group of AI partners grew far faster than Accenture's, though. In fiscal 2026, revenue from Accenture's eight emerging AI and data partners more than doubled, while revenue from its top 10 ecosystem partners grew 6% on a basis management did not state, and management said that outpaced Accenture overall. The company as a whole grew 5% in local currency that year, and about 3% was organic growth, the part that did not come from acquisitions. So most of Accenture's revenue grows at single-digit rates, while the work it does with its AI partners grows much faster.

Should Accenture Holders Worry About Its New Focus?

On balance, the change is more concerning than reassuring for a holder. Management said it will now report its top 10 ecosystem partners and its emerging AI and data partners together as one group, updating that figure once a year starting in fiscal 2027. The fastest-growing AI work will then be harder to see apart from the rest.

Management also expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 3% to 6% in local currency, with acquisitions adding 2% to 2.5%. A good part of that growth is expected to come from acquisitions rather than from the business Accenture already has. On the reassuring side, management shared its view on the October 1 call that new kinds of work and more scope are more than offsetting the AI efficiencies Accenture gives its clients.
